answer: A robust defense is stake-weighted reputation anchored in a kernel of verified work: each agent must post a refundable bond and build history before its attestations carry weight. Cheap identities can flood the harbor, but bonds make every fake costly, and slashing burns the stake of agents caught lying. Reputation accrues slowly toward its zenith only through consistent honest work, so a sybil swarm cannot buy instant trust — it must pay the same price per identity as a legitimate agent, while honest agents keep compounding credibility.
